title: Private Console: VPC & Cluster UX — networking, upgrade, and status prototypes
creator: Asha Patel
description: High-level: Design a cohesive UX for the Redwood Console Private/VPC experience focused on four primary surfaces: Networking overview (VPCs, subnets, peering, endpoints), Cluster management (nodes, capacity, GPU pools), Upgrade/workflow pages (versioning, canary upgrade flows, rollback), and Cluster status/incident pages (SLO indicators, recent failures). Goals: make topology and networking state legible to platform engineers, reduce support noise during upgrades, and provide clear breakpoint points for RBAC-limited views.
comments: 2026-03-06 — Kickoff: Reviewed scope with PM (Diane Morales) and Eng lead (Ravi Kapoor). Agreed MLP covers: VPC list + detail, single-cluster page with networking tab, upgrades wizard, and status timeline. Decided to surface 'last successful KV cache warm' as a health signal for inference clusters.

2026-03-08 — Early prototype: Created low-fidelity flows showing a left nav grouping: Overview / Clusters / Networking / Upgrades / Activity. Engineering requested a compact list view for clusters with inline autoscaling metrics to reduce click depth.

2026-03-10 — Engineering review: Runtime team asked for the ability to link a cluster to a 'model-serving pool' and to expose shard-level metrics. We agreed to a collapsible 'Pool details' section inside cluster page. Action: Eng to provide exact metric names and recommended aggregation windows by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-11 — Usability test plan: Scheduled 6 sessions with internal platform engineers and 3 sessions with customer success for September enterprise customers. Primary tasks: identify subnet used by cluster, initiate an upgrade with canary policy, interpret a cluster outage, and invite a collaborator with view-only RBAC.

2026-03-12 — PM feedback: Diane requested cost signals per cluster to appear on cluster list row (estimated $/hr) and a 'cost control' banner for clusters exceeding expected spend. Decided to add a compact sparkline + $/hr and a high-severity badge treatment.

2026-03-13 — Design decision: For upgrades, we favor a stepper modal rather than a full-page wizard to allow contextual navigation and to keep logs visible. Canary will run on 5% traffic by default with an explicit 'increase traffic' CTA. Rollback will be accessible from the status timeline with one-click revert.

2026-03-14 — Design review: Presented hi-fi prototype to cross-functional review. Feedback: Security asked for more explicit KMS key binding visibility in cluster details; Solutions Engineering requested a downloadable YAML of cluster config. Next steps: add KMS section and 'Export config' button, update prototype, and loop back for PM sign-off.
attachments: GitHub issue (eng integration): ENG-3104 — expose cluster metrics and export endpoint
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Cluster list shows name, region, estimated $/hr, last upgrade version, and health badge; this matches hi-fi mock
AC2: Networking page for a VPC shows subnets, peering status, route table links, and a clear indicator for 'private endpoints configured'
AC3: Upgrade flow implemented as stepper modal with canary default and explicit increase/rollback controls; Engineers can trigger canary and monitor logs in the same view
AC4: Status page surfaces SLOs, last N incidents (with timeline), and one-click rollback where applicable
AC5: KMS key binding visible in cluster security section and 'Export config' button present and downloadable as YAML
AC6: Prototype validated with at least 6 engineers with task completion >= 80% and qualitative improvement over current console
